- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak if sentiment >0.75.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases; apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.6.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.2x recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15% if sentiment <0.5; if <0.8x, increase by 5–10% if sentiment >0.7.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 1–3 days; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment >0.65 to compensate for lag.
